speaker: Unknown
en: I told the team yesterday that the real cost of this 1.2 billion was not dilution.
zh: 我昨天跟团队说，这 12 亿的真正代价不是股权稀释。

speaker: Unknown
en: The real cost is expectations, not only from our investors, because I think our investors, they understood and they agree on the long-term vision of the company, but the expectations you create in the outside world, and if you raise 1 billion and you do nothing for two years, or people don't see anything coming out of it for two years, then it's very, very hard to survive.
zh: 真正的代价是期望，不仅来自我们的投资人，因为我觉得我们的投资人理解并且认同公司的长期愿景，而是你在外部世界创造的期望，如果你融了 10 亿然后两年什么都不做，或者大家两年都看不到任何产出，那你要活下来就非常、非常难。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we actually met Alex.
zh: 所以我们其实见过 Alex。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fun fact, we actually did the same YC batch.
zh: 有个有趣的事实，我们其实是同一期 YC 的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back then, Alex was building WeetAI, and we were building Algolia.
zh: 当时，Alex 在做 WeetAI，我们在做 Algolia。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was in winter 2014, quite a while ago, except Alex has done four companies.
zh: 那是 2014 年冬天，挺久以前了，只不过 Alex 已经做过四家公司了。

speaker: Unknown
en: One before, two after.
zh: 之前一家，之后两家。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've only done one, so I cannot compare.
zh: 我只做过一家，所以没法比较。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm super impressed by all your background and everything you've done.
zh: 所以我对你的背景和你做成的一切印象非常深刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you remember from Wit?
zh: 你对 Wit 还记得什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Wit.ai, was that the first AI company or something?
zh: Wit.ai，那是第一家 AI 公司还是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it was the first .ai domain, actually.
zh: 对，它其实是第一个 .ai 域名。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was very hard back then to buy .ai.
zh: 那时候买 .ai 域名非常难。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an island of Australia.
zh: 那是澳大利亚的一个岛。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you know about it or did you find it by chance?
zh: 你本来就知道，还是偶然发现的？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I found this and I thought, oh, it would be cool to have this domain, but nobody understood it was a domain back in early 2013.
zh: 不是，我是偶然发现的，我心想，哦，能拿到这个域名会很酷，但在 2013 年初，没人明白那是个域名。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's how old we are.
zh: 我们就是这么老的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I was surprised because actually you sold WIT shortly after to Facebook, right?
zh: 然后我很惊讶，因为你其实在之后不久就把 WIT 卖给了 Facebook，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: How did that go?
zh: 那是怎么回事？

speaker: Unknown
en: Any memory of that time?
zh: 对那段时期有什么记忆吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so in 2015 I received actually an email from someone called Mark Zuckerberg.
zh: 有，2015 年的时候，我收到了一封来自一个叫 Mark Zuckerberg 的人的邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And after like half a second, I deleted the email without opening it.
zh: 大概半秒之后，我没打开就把邮件删了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a scam, you know, it's a spam.
zh: 是诈骗嘛，你知道，是垃圾邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I took about half an hour and then I thought, oh, but maybe it isn't, you know, I should check.
zh: 过了大概半个小时，我心想，哦，但也许不是呢，你知道，我应该查一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I opened my spam folder and it wasn't, so it started like that.
zh: 然后我打开垃圾邮件文件夹，发现不是，事情就是这么开始的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what happened after?
zh: 那之后发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you met him, like it was real, you met him and he made an offer?
zh: 比如你见了他，比如是真的，你见了他然后他开了报价？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, is that it?
zh: 是这样吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So we actually followed the YC playbook.
zh: 所以我们其实遵循了 YC 的剧本。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you're not supposed to...
zh: 你知道，你不应该……

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't want to sell, don't speak with them.
zh: 如果你不想卖，就不要跟他们谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you're not supposed to speak to anyone.
zh: 对，你不应该跟任何人谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: As soon as you start a startup, you receive lots of offer to talk.
zh: 你一创办创业公司，就会收到很多要聊的邀约。

speaker: Unknown
en: But usually these are from the corporate development of large companies and they need to talk to everyone to understand the market and they need to know...
zh: 但通常这些来自大公司的企业发展部门，他们需要跟所有人聊来了解市场，他们需要知道……

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're desperate enough to sell for a low price.
zh: 你是不是已经绝望到愿意低价卖掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's a very bad idea to waste your time and your attention.
zh: 所以浪费你的时间和注意力是非常糟糕的主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: So YC tells you never talk to anyone unless you are selling your company.
zh: 所以 YC 告诉你，除非你要卖公司，否则不要跟任何人谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unless you want to sell.
zh: 除非你想卖。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that was not the corporate, I mean, or maybe the corporate arm of Facebook was so smart they got Mark to send the email.
zh: 但那不是企业发展部门，我是说，或者也许 Facebook 的企业发展部门太聪明了，他们让 Mark 来发那封邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: If someone really has the power to do something big, maybe, and you can talk.
zh: 如果某个人真的有权力做大事，也许，你就可以谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: So tell us what was, in a way, it feels like all your companies were very early in what they were doing.
zh: 那么说说，从某种角度看，感觉你所有的公司在自己做的事情上都非常早。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like Virtuos was already conversationally just right before that name even existed.
zh: 比如 Virtuos 在对话式这个词甚至存在之前就已经在做对话式了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this one was really, really too early.
zh: 所以这一家真的是、真的太早了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But WIT was also early.
zh: 但 WIT 也早。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which was not that early.
zh: 那倒没那么早。

speaker: Unknown
en: My first company, almost out of school, was a chatbot company.
zh: 我的第一家公司，几乎是刚出校门，是一家聊天机器人公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I started in 2002, so you are not born.
zh: 我是 2002 年开始的，所以你还没出生。

speaker: Unknown
en: 20 years too early.
zh: 早了 20 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, 20 years too early.
zh: 对，早了 20 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: But still, we made it, you know, we made something with it.
zh: 但尽管如此，我们还是做成了，你知道，我们用它做出了点东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then people ask, and so I'm trying to sell chatbots for customer service in 2002.
zh: 但后来人们会问,当时我在 2002 年 trying to sell 用于客服的聊天机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people ask me, but what is a chatbot?
zh: 人们问我,但什么是聊天机器人?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I say, it's like a live chat.
zh: 我说,就像在线聊天一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's automatic.
zh: 但它是自动的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to say, but what is live chat?
zh: 然后他们说,但什么是在线聊天?

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was really, really too early.
zh: 所以当时真的、真的太早了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we spent 10 years with this company.
zh: 我们在这家公司花了 10 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: We survived long enough to, and then there was actually a market in 2010 as a nascent market, but it was definitely too early.
zh: 我们撑得够久,然后 2010 年确实出现了一个市场,一个新兴市场,但当时肯定还是太早了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you sold Viatros, you sold WIT, then you spent a lot of time at Meta, and then you created a third company, Nabla, and then at last AmiLabs.
zh: 所以你卖掉了 Viatros,卖掉了 WIT,然后你在 Meta 花了很多时间,接着你创建了第三家公司 Nabla,最后是 AmiLabs。

speaker: Unknown
en: Was that earlier this year?
zh: 那是今年早些时候的事吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, in January.
zh: 是的,1 月份。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like every single of these companies was kind of early.
zh: 感觉你每一家公司都有点太早了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even AmiLabs, right?
zh: 甚至 AmiLabs 也是,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: In a way, you are going after a big new approach to AI that could feel very early today.
zh: 某种程度上,你们在追求一种全新的 AI 路径,今天来看可能感觉非常早。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that something that's in you?
zh: 它只是非常、非常昂贵,因为如果你想构建一个财务模型,你需要买成千上万块 GPU。

speaker: Unknown
en: You always want to really...
zh: 你总是想要真正……

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it depends what is your strengths.
zh: 我觉得这取决于你的优势是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: If your strengths as co-founders are either go-to-market, sales, you know, marketing, then you shouldn't be too early.
zh: 如果你作为联合创始人的优势是市场推广、销售、营销之类的,那你就不应该太早。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need a product to be ready.
zh: 你需要产品已经就绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need the market to be ready to receive your go-to-market.
zh: 你需要市场已经准备好接收你的市场推广。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if your strength is to push a product to the market, then being too early will kill you.
zh: 所以如果你的优势是把产品推向市场,那么太早会害死你。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think my strengths and I think
zh: 我觉得我的优势是,而且我觉得

speaker: Unknown
en: Usually it's a cliche, but in France, probably, you know, we are most famous for engineering and tech more than genius of marketing and sales.
zh: 通常这是老生常谈,但在法国,我们最出名的可能是工程和技术,而不是营销和销售方面的天才。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in my case, I think what I like to do is take very, very early tech and think about what product, how we can sell it through a product, build this product, understand the early market.
zh: 所以就我而言,我觉得我喜欢做的事情是拿非常、非常早期的技术,思考什么样的产品、我们如何通过产品把它卖出去,构建这个产品,理解早期市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think my skills are more on the early side of the go-to market.
zh: 所以我觉得我的技能更多在市场推广偏早期的那一端。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's why I prefer to take early ideas.
zh: 所以这就是为什么我更喜欢做早期的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it really depends on what you want to focus on.
zh: 但这真的取决于你想专注在什么上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's continue with AmiLabs.
zh: 我们继续聊 AmiLabs。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like it's the most ambitious project ever for you, right?
zh: 感觉这是你有史以来最雄心勃勃的项目,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the first one were normal startups.
zh: 我是说,前几个都是普通创业公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: This one is not really normal.
zh: 这一个真的不太普通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what led you to actually take that leap?
zh: 比如,是什么让你真正迈出了那一步?

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I mean, it's a normal project.
zh: 所以,我是说,这是个正常的项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just very, very expensive because if you want to build a financial model, you need to buy thousands and thousands of GPUs.
zh: 这非常非常昂贵,因为如果你想构建一个财务模型,你需要购买成千上万块 GPU。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you need billions of euros.
zh: 所以你需要几十亿欧元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is what is not normal in this project.
zh: 所以这就是这个项目不正常的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've done several startups, always on the applied AI space.
zh: 我做过好几家创业公司,一直在应用 AI 领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm using machine learning research or models that other people have done.
zh: 也就是说,我是在使用别人做出来的机器学习研究或模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And after all this year, having the opportunity to work upstream on the model that if we are successful, millions of people will use is very exciting.
zh: 而经过这么多年,有机会在上游工作,做那个如果我们成功的话数百万人会使用的模型,是非常令人兴奋的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So moving upstream is what I think is the most exciting.
zh: 所以向上游移动是我觉得最令人兴奋的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How many here know what a world model is?
zh: 在座有多少人知道什么是世界模型?

speaker: Unknown
en: I like more than I would expect.
zh: 我很喜欢,比我预期的多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had to research it myself just to make sure I understood what you were doing.
zh: 我自己都得去研究一下,就是为了确保我理解你们在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it's kind of like a very different take at the market than like LLMs are kind of like the one thing, right?
zh: 因为这和 LLM 是相当不同的市场切入点,LLM 就像是唯一的那个东西,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So in a way it's been contrarian for a while.
zh: 所以某种程度上,这已经逆势了一段时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why wouldn't LLM do everything?
zh: 为什么 LLM 不能包办一切?

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you tell us a little more about what is the world model and what's your kind of like your bet on the market?
zh: 你能多讲一点什么是世界模型,以及你们对市场的押注是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so first I'm happy to see that many people have heard about it.
zh: 是的,首先我很高兴看到很多人听说过它。

speaker: Unknown
en: How many were honest?
zh: 有多少人是诚实的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: So my co-founder, Yann Lequin, speaks often, so maybe... You'll hear about him.
zh: 我的联合创始人 Yann Lequin 经常演讲，所以也许……你会听到关于他的消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: So basically, as you know, a large language model learns to manipulate language.
zh: 基本上，如你所知，一个大语言模型学习操纵语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you can read... NLM will be trained by reading all the texts, all the books, all the internets in the world.
zh: 所以你可以读到……NLM 会通过阅读所有的文本、所有的书、世界上所有的互联网来训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so LLM is learning what we humans have written about the world.
zh: 所以 LLM 学的是我们人类写下的关于世界的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a kind of proxy.
zh: 所以它是一种代理。

speaker: Unknown
en: LLM doesn't learn directly from the world, the real world.
zh: LLM 不是直接从世界、从现实世界学习的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We humans have wrote books and articles about the world, and then the LLM learns this text.
zh: 我们人类写了关于世界的书和文章，然后 LLM 学习这些文本。

speaker: Unknown
en: LLM is like someone who has never gone outside, never left the room they were born in.
zh: LLM 就像一个从来没有出过门、从未离开过自己出生的那个房间的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But read all the books every day for centuries and centuries.
zh: 但几个世纪以来每天读所有的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this person seems like an expert on many things, but with no direct experience of the world, will have limited common sense and limited ability actually to find new solutions or to know what to do when facing a situation for the first time, lacking the direct world experience.
zh: 所以这个人看起来像很多方面的专家，但没有对世界的直接经验，常识会很有限，真正找到新解法的能力、或者在第一次面对某种情况时知道该做什么的能力也会很有限，因为缺乏直接的世界经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: A world model is a model where we don't cheat.
zh: 世界模型是一个我们不作弊的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are not learning through text.
zh: 我们不是通过文本来学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are learning directly like humans, like animals from the real world.
zh: 我们像人类、像动物一样，直接从现实世界学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: So meaning video, audio, sensory data, playing with objects.
zh: 意思是视频、音频、感官数据、把玩物体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we are really starting from scratch, like a baby, without any language.
zh: 所以我们真的是从零开始，像婴儿一样，没有任何语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what's the training data?
zh: 那训练数据是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What kind of training data are you using?
zh: 你们用的是什么样的训练数据？

speaker: Unknown
en: We are using a lot of video data because it's easiest to find, but it works with audio.
zh: 我们用大量的视频数据，因为它最容易找到，但音频也行。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would work with only, like, if you were born without sight or hearing, you can still live.
zh: 即使用……比如如果你生来没有视觉或听觉，你仍然可以活着。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's possible to live through touch, and it's the same in what we do.
zh: 所以靠触觉生活是可能的，我们所做的事情也一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you collect touch data?
zh: 你们能采集触觉数据吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you do that?
zh: 怎么做的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Through robotics.
zh: 通过机器人技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So once you get that model, what are the use cases?
zh: 那一旦你有了那个模型，用例是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What can it do that an LLM cannot do?
zh: 它能做什么 LLM 做不到的事？

speaker: Unknown
en: So in the short term, there are lots of applications, especially in robotics.
zh: 短期来看，有很多应用，尤其是在机器人领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: Current robots are very, very narrow, vertical robots.
zh: 当前的机器人非常非常窄，是垂直的机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They do one thing in one position, and it takes a lot of time to train them to do only one thing, always the same.
zh: 它们在一个位置只做一件事，而且要花很多时间训练它们只做一件事，总是一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are not ready at all to have this robot be in an open environment, whether it's in your house or in the street or, you know, and you see these videos of robots that start to dance and break everything around or I don't know if you've seen the one where a robot is doing a karate demonstration and does like that and there is a child and the child is...
zh: 我们完全没有准备好让这种机器人待在开放环境里，无论是在你家还是在街上，你知道的，你见过那些机器人开始跳舞然后把周围一切都打坏的视频，或者我不知道你有没有见过那个机器人做空手道演示然后这样挥过去，旁边有个小孩，那个小孩就……

speaker: Unknown
en: So these robots are very, very dumb.
zh: 所以这些机器人非常非常笨。

speaker: Unknown
en: The hardware is incredibly evolved, but the brain hasn't changed.
zh: 硬件进化得令人难以置信，但大脑没有变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you cannot take these robots in an open environment.
zh: 而且你不能把这些机器人带进开放环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wouldn't be safe and they wouldn't be useful.
zh: 那不安全，它们也不会有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is a first application.
zh: 所以这是第一个应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: How does that differ from VLAs, for example?
zh: 那和 VLA 之类的东西有什么不同？

speaker: Unknown
en: VLA is a very bad hack where you have a hammer, you have a LLM, and you see everything as a nail.
zh: VLA 是一个非常糟糕的 hack：你有一把锤子，你有一个 LLM，然后你看什么都像钉子。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are trying to use your solution for things that it was not designed for.
zh: 你在试图把你的方案用在与它设计初衷不符的事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a VLA is not accurate.
zh: 所以 VLA 不精确。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very slow, but you need very fast, very short latency to do these applications, and it's very expensive.
zh: 它非常慢，但这些应用需要非常快、非常短的延迟，而且它非常昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: You cannot pay $100 of compute for 24 hours of your home robot to work.
zh: 你不可能为家里机器人工作 24 小时支付 100 美元的算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there are many, many problems with VLA.
zh: 所以 VLA 有很多很多问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, like, word models are a better solution.
zh: 所以，世界模型是更好的解法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they easy, like, in terms of inference?
zh: 它们在推理方面容易吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they costly?
zh: 成本高吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can they be real-time?
zh: 能做到实时吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So they are very costly to train, like LLMs, hence, you know, the GPUs we have to train.
zh: 它们的训练成本非常高，和 LLM 一样，所以，你知道的，我们要用 GPU 来训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: More or the same?
zh: 更多还是差不多？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's comparable.
zh: 差不多。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hard to compare because it's not the same structure or the same.
zh: 很难比较，因为结构不一样，也不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when they are trained, they are supposed to be more lightweight for several reasons, but you have less parameters.
zh: 但它们训练出来时，按理说会更轻量，原因有几个，比如参数更少。

speaker: Unknown
en: So inference should be less expensive.
zh: 所以推理应该更便宜。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

en: In the world where world models are in production everywhere, what is still good for LLMs?
zh: 在世界模型到处都在生产环境使用的世界里，LLM 还有什么是擅长的？

en: Is that the one replace the other?
zh: 是一个取代另一个吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, no, I'm not saying the LLMs are not good.
zh: 不，不，我不是说 LLM 不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: LLMs are already very, very good, as we all know, for everything that is language first, everything that is a sequence of symbols, like discrete and low dimension problems, so anything with language, mathematics, programming,
zh: LLM 已经非常非常好了，众所周知，对于一切以语言为先的东西，一切符号序列的东西，比如离散的低维问题，所以任何涉及语言、数学、编程的，

speaker: Unknown
en: These are all low-dimensional sequence of symbols.
zh: 这些都是低维的符号序列。

speaker: Unknown
en: LLMs are designed for that.
zh: LLM 就是为这些设计的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We will never beat, I think, the LLM at that.
zh: 我认为在这些方面我们永远无法击败 LLM。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then you have lots of high-dimensional, very noisy, very long-horizon problems for which we think world models will be vastly superior.
zh: 但还有很多高维、非常嘈杂、非常长时程的问题，我们认为世界模型会远远优于 LLM。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're speaking a lot about the future.
zh: 所以我们谈了很多未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there already world models in prod?
zh: 现在已经有世界模型在生产环境里了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Got some flavor of it, at least?
zh: 哪怕有一些雏形？

speaker: Unknown
en: There are some ideas behind world models in production.
zh: 生产环境里有一些世界模型背后的理念在应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: For instance, some autonomous driving companies are using some flavors.
zh: 比如一些自动驾驶公司正在使用某些雏形。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is Waymo using a world model?
zh: Waymo 在用世界模型吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Some flavor of, and Wave also in the UK.
zh: 某种雏形，还有英国的 Wave 也是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of the ideas we are using, like JEPA, have been around for at least five, ten years.
zh: 我们在用的一些理念，比如 JEPA，已经存在至少五到十年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know what happened in 2018?
zh: 你知道 2018 年发生了什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The theoretical idea behind LLM, like Transformers, the paper was there, but Google did nothing with it.
zh: LLM 背后的理论，比如 Transformer，论文已经在了，但 Google 什么也没做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody did anything with it.
zh: 谁也没拿它做任何事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody realized the power.
zh: 没有人意识到它的威力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that the pattern?
zh: 是同样的模式吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then OpenAI, you know, we can criticize OpenAI for many reasons, but they took this and scaled it, solved some engineering, you know, scaling issues.
zh: 然后 OpenAI，你知道，我们可以因为很多理由批评 OpenAI，但他们拿起了这个并把它规模化，解决了一些工程问题，你知道的，一些规模化问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: DeepMind is meta today, because it was developed there at first.
zh: DeepMind 今天是 Meta 的，因为它最初是在那里开发的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think all the large companies back then, you know, Meta, I was at Meta, so I know exactly.
zh: 我认为当时所有的大公司，你知道，Meta，我当时在 Meta，所以我一清二楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are many reasons why in a large company, there are things you cannot do that as a startup you can't do.
zh: 在大公司里有很多原因导致有些事你做不了，而作为初创公司你可以做。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can take lots of risk.
zh: 你可以冒很多险。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't take any risk, you're dead because the big companies have more resources than you.
zh: 如果你一点险都不冒，你就死了，因为大公司比你资源多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they have a brand, and they have many, many things you don't have.
zh: 而且他们有品牌，他们有很多很多你没有的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the one thing you have that they don't is the ability to make crazy things, to take some risks.
zh: 但你有一件他们没有的东西：做出疯狂事情的能力，去冒一些险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason, when I was at Meta, for instance, we worked on a chatbot, which was a language model, not large yet, you know, but the ID that we trained... Just out of We.ai?
zh: 举个例子，我在 Meta 的时候，我们做过一个聊天机器人，它是一个语言模型，当时还不算大，你知道，但我们训练它的想法是……是不是出自 We.ai？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, but trained statistically without rules, but trained from statistical data.
zh: 是的，但它是用统计方法训练的，没有规则，而是从统计数据中训练的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We worked a lot.
zh: 我们投入了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had a lot of fun.
zh: 我们玩得很开心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the first time we launched a chatbot in the lab at Meta, we asked a question, how are you today?
zh: 第一次我们在 Meta 实验室里上线这个聊天机器人时，我们问了一个问题，你今天怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the chatbot answered, oh, just chilling, watching porn on my couch.
zh: 聊天机器人回答，哦，就在放松，躺在我沙发上看黄片。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, before that, I wanted to release this chatbot.
zh: 而在那之前，我想发布这个聊天机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I thought, okay, the legal team, you know, they will never, ever want to have this discussion with me.
zh: 然后我想，好吧，法务团队，你知道，他们绝对、绝对不想跟我讨论这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we knew we cannot release it.
zh: 所以我们知道我们没法发布它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just an example.
zh: 这只是一个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so OpenAI could take some risks with GPT-1, 2, 3, you know, until chat GPT-1.
zh: 而 OpenAI 可以用 GPT-1、2、3 冒一些险，你知道，直到 ChatGPT-1。

speaker: Unknown
en: That no one else could, so they have the ability to, they have enough money and resources to scale the training, but the ability to take risk, because they had this combination, they made it what became ChatGPT.
zh: 这是别人都做不到的，所以他们有能力，他们有足够的钱和资源去扩大训练规模，但也有冒风险的能力，因为他们有这个组合，才造就了后来的 ChatGPT。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, just to finish on that, like, what's the current bottleneck?
zh: 那么最后，就这个问题收个尾，目前的瓶颈是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that training data then?
zh: 是训练数据吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need three things.
zh: 你需要三样东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need smart people, you know, talents, to understand because not so many people, you know, understand that.
zh: 你需要聪明人，你知道，人才，去理解，因为没有多少人，你知道，理解这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of them are working on LLMs.
zh: 他们中的大多数都在做 LLM。

speaker: Unknown
en: And most of them are LLM-peeled, like Yann says.
zh: 而且它们大多数都是被 LLM 剥离过的，就像 Yann 说的那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need a lot of data, and you need GPUs, compute, which is very, even when you have money, it's very, very hard to secure GPUs.
zh: 你需要大量数据，你需要 GPU、算力，这非常，即使你有钱，要 securing GPU 也非常非常难。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now, you've already hired quite a lot of talents, and you've raised a lot of money.
zh: 那么现在，你已经招了相当多的人才，也融了很多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what's left?
zh: 那还缺什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Data?
zh: 数据？

speaker: Unknown
en: Data and compute.
zh: 数据和算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even with money, securing compute today is difficult.
zh: 即使有钱，如今 securing 算力也很困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of like a contrarian bet.
zh: 这有点像一场反共识的赌注。

speaker: Unknown
en: What convinced you to bet everything on it?
zh: 是什么让你决定把一切都押在上面的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't think it's contrarian.
zh: 我不认为这是反共识。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was maybe contrarian a year ago, but I think it's becoming less and less.
zh: 一年前也许算反共识，但我认为它正变得越来越不是了。

speaker: Unknown
en: A year ago, when we were saying LLMs are nice and powerful, but they're not AGI.
zh: 一年前，当我们在说 LLM 很不错很强大，但它们不是 AGI。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't lead to artificial, you know, general or super intelligence.
zh: 它们不会通向人工，你知道的，通用或超级智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most people disagree now.
zh: 现在大多数人都不同意了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think most people agree that LLMs don't lead, maybe not most people, but a good chunk of people agree that LLMs don't lead to general intelligence.
zh: 我认为大多数人同意，也许不是大多数人，但相当一部分人同意，LLM 不会通向通用智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now you can disagree on what leads to...
zh: 所以现在你可以对什么通向……产生分歧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the definition is also fuzzy.
zh: 我是说，定义本身也是模糊的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fact that the definition has changed.
zh: 事实上定义已经变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the very people who promised AGI changed the definition and stopped using the term.
zh: 所以正是那些当初承诺 AGI 的人改变了定义，并且不再使用这个术语。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a good sign that something is not working.
zh: 我认为这是某件事行不通的好迹象。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're doing that with Yann and you met Yann at Meta, I guess?
zh: 而你是在和 Yann 一起做这件事，我猜你是在 Meta 认识 Yann 的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yes, of course.
zh: 所以是的，当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're working with him before.
zh: 所以你之前就和他共事过。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you kind of like knew him enough.
zh: 所以你算是足够了解他。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did that go?
zh: 那是怎么开始的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, did he coach you for the job?
zh: 比如，他有没有为这个职位辅导过你？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, how did you end up working together?
zh: 比如，你们最后是怎么一起共事的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So Jan was an investor and advisor in Nabla, my company prior to AmiLabs.
zh: Jan 是 Nabla 的投资人和顾问，那是我在 AmiLabs 之前的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I saw him very often.
zh: 所以我经常见到他。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one day he came to me and said, Hey Alex, I think world models are ready to become very big.
zh: 有一天他来找我说，嘿 Alex，我认为 world models 已经准备好变得非常大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we could go faster if we do that outside of Meta.
zh: 而且我认为如果我们 Meta 之外做这件事，可以更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: As an autonomous startup.
zh: 作为一个独立初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want to do it.
zh: 所以我想做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I need a CEO.
zh: 而我需要一个 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: So... Are you up for it?
zh: 所以……你愿意吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, you know, I spent... My first company was doing chatbots, as I said, and after 10 years trying to teach a machine to understand human language and concepts for customer support, my conclusion was we cannot cheat.
zh: 是的，我是说，你知道，我花了……我的第一家公司是做聊天机器人的，就像我说过的，在花了 10 年试图教机器理解人类语言和概念以做客服之后，我的结论是我们不能作弊。

speaker: Unknown
en: We cannot... A machine can speak about a cat.
zh: 我们不能……机器可以谈论猫。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if the machine has never seen a cat, you know, touched a cat, played with a cat, maybe be hurt by a cat, then it will never be very, very smart.
zh: 但如果机器从未见过猫，你知道，摸过猫、和猫玩过、也许被猫弄伤过，那它永远也不会非常非常聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we talk about a cat, it actually reactivates in our brain some past experience we had with cats.
zh: 当我们谈论猫时，它实际上会激活我们大脑中我们与猫有过的一些过往经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is my... And even if you read a book...
zh: 这是我的……即使你读了一本书……

speaker: Unknown
en: about some animals like that you've never, like a dinosaur, like never seen.
zh: 关于某种动物，比如你从未见过的，比如恐龙，比如从未见过。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way you imagine the dinosaur is built on basic objects that you had experience with.
zh: 你想象恐龙的方式是建立在你有过的基本物体的经验之上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you go, you know, what we call grounding, you need real experience of things to be smart.
zh: 所以如果你去，你知道，我们所说的 grounding，你需要对事物有真实的经验才能变得聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is my, it was my belief before 10 years ago.
zh: 这是我的，这是我 10 年前的信念。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just need to see a Justin Park and you're good.
zh: 只需要见一下 Justin Park 你就搞定了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you split responsibilities then?
zh: 那你们是怎么分工的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because he's still the inventor, the researcher who came up with that JPA thing.
zh: 因为他仍然是发明者,是提出那个 JPA 东西的研究者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you more on the execution side, making sure we can build the product out of it?
zh: 你是不是更多在执行这一边,确保我们能把它做成产品?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you split the whole thing?
zh: 你们是怎么划分整件事的?

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, Jens is the executive chairman of the company.
zh: 是的,Jens 是公司的执行董事长。

speaker: Unknown
en: He has a scientific vision.
zh: 他有科学上的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he's leading the direction of the research.
zh: 所以他负责领导研究的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then my job is to make sure that there are people, we have electricity, GPUs, data, office.
zh: 而我的工作是确保有人、我们有电、GPU、数据、办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if it fails, it's because of you.
zh: 所以如果失败了,那是因为你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything is working, of course.
zh: 当然,一切都在正常运转。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I love this.
zh: 而且我很喜欢这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, it's very hard to manage researchers.
zh: 另外,管理研究者是非常难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, there is a joke that it's like herding cats.
zh: 你知道,有个笑话说是像放猫一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to leave.
zh: 你必须放手。

speaker: Unknown
en: You cannot tell researchers what to do.
zh: 你不能告诉研究者该做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: They hate that they will flee if you try.
zh: 他们讨厌那样,如果你试图这样做他们会跑掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: But on the other hand, if you leave researchers alone, they will just do very random things and run in all directions and you will never get anything of them.
zh: 但另一方面,如果你放任研究者不管,他们就会做非常随机的事情,朝所有方向乱跑,你永远也得不到任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so finding the very, very tight balance between direction, enough direction with enough freedom, I think, in order to get a product one day, is what I like to do.
zh: 所以在方向与自由之间找到非常、非常精准的平衡——足够的方向配足够的自由,我认为,是为了有一天能做出产品——这正是我喜欢做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Excellent.
zh: 很好。

en: You also ended up raising the biggest ever seed round in Europe, right?
zh: 你们还完成了欧洲有史以来最大的种子轮融资,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like 1.2 billion, is that in dollars?

speaker: Unknown
en: In dollars.
zh: 是美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: In dollars, okay.
zh: 美元,好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, close, like 1 billion in euros, right?
zh: 嗯,差不多,大概 10 亿欧元,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Walk us through that.

en: Like first, maybe, could you ever imagine raising that much money?

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I could never imagine, I think no one could imagine a few years ago that any startup would need so much seed money.
zh: 不,我从来无法想象,我想几年前没人能想象任何初创公司会需要这么多种子资金。

speaker: Unknown
en: The real craziness is the cost of compute, and because you need a lot of compute, you need a lot of money, and then everything has shifted.
zh: 真正疯狂的是算力的成本,因为你需要很多算力,你就需要很多钱,然后一切都变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, this is...
zh: 是的,这是……

speaker: Unknown
en: A new territory for everyone.
zh: 对每个人来说都是新领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's difficult is when you start a company, I think having a culture of not spending too much money, be very careful, spend money as if it's yours, is very, very important for the company.
zh: 困难的是,当你创办一家公司,我认为建立一种不花太多钱的文化,非常谨慎,把钱当成自己的钱来花,对公司来说非常、非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very hard to change later if you don't start like that, being very cautious with money.
zh: 如果你不那样开始、对钱非常谨慎的话,以后要改变是非常难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's hard, because if you spend one billion for GPUs, then everything else looks very cheap.

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's very tempting to... And how about finding the money?

speaker: Unknown
en: Was that easier than expected?

speaker: Unknown
en: It was not that hard, actually.

en: You should aim for billions, not millions.

speaker: Unknown
en: The difficulty doesn't depend on the amount, it depends on if it's your first time.
zh: 难度不取决于金额,取决于是不是你的第一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, of course.

en: I don't think anyone else could have done that.

en: Just the way I see that helps.

speaker: Unknown
en: Second time is easy.

en: And then after a third time, people just beg you to give you money to do anything you want.

speaker: Unknown
en: So, but you have to go through this journey.

speaker: Unknown
en: And because the first few times were successful, that helps too, I guess.

en: Yeah.

en: Yeah.

en: I mean, a seed with that size, like kind of like probably set expectations before you even start working.

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, does that money buy you, buys you patience or
zh: 我是说，这笔钱是买来了耐心，还是

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it put you on the clock?
zh: 是不是把你放到了倒计时上？

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, I told the team yesterday that the real cost of this 1.2 billion was not dilution.
zh: 其实，我昨天跟团队说，这 12 亿的真正成本不是股权稀释。

speaker: Unknown
en: The real cost is expectations, not only from our investors, because I think our investors, they understood and they agree on the long-term vision of the company.
zh: 真正的成本是预期，不仅是来自投资人的，因为我觉得我们的投资人理解并认同公司的长期愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the expectations you create in the outside world, and if you raise 1 billion and you do nothing for two years, or people don't see anything coming out of it for two years, then it's very, very hard to survive.
zh: 而是你在外部世界制造的预期，如果你融了 10 亿然后两年什么都没做，或者人们两年看不到任何产出，那就非常非常难生存下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the expectations is much harder.
zh: 所以预期这一块要难得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And do you have a timeline?
zh: 那你们有时间表吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like maybe you don't want to share?
zh: 也许你不想分享？

speaker: Unknown
en: You see expectations coming.
zh: 你看到预期来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: You raised a lot.
zh: 你融了很多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now you have to... Internally, we have a timeline.
zh: 现在你必须……内部上，我们是有时间表的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you going to see anything this year?
zh: 今年能看到什么成果吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't communicate about it.
zh: 我们不对外沟通这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I tried.
zh: 我试过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I tried.
zh: 我试过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you do that here in Paris, where pretty much nearly everyone else is building these labs in SF.
zh: 而且你是在巴黎做这件事，而几乎其他所有人都在 SF 建这些实验室。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why Paris?
zh: 为什么是巴黎？

speaker: Unknown
en: So we do this in Paris.
zh: 我们在巴黎做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have a big team in New York, one in Montreal and one in Singapore.
zh: 我们在纽约也有个大团队，蒙特利尔有一个，新加坡有一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have these four cities because we had existing teams.
zh: 我们有这四个城市，因为我们本来就有现成的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't hear SF.
zh: 我没听到 SF。

speaker: Unknown
en: And no SF, so it's a kind of… That's the contrarian bet too?
zh: 对，没有 SF，所以这是一种……这也是反主流的押注吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: A little bit, yeah.
zh: 有一点吧，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's when people join AMI, we hire lots of people in SF, in the companies you can imagine.
zh: 我觉得当人们加入 AMI 时，我们招了很多 SF 的人，来自你能想到的那些公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have to move to New York.
zh: 他们必须搬到纽约。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like a commitment and it's very important at this early stage to have people who join with a real commitment and not just because they want to try.
zh: 这就像一种承诺，在这么早期的阶段，让人们带着真正的承诺加入，而不是只想试试，这非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's half, one day we'll have an office over there, but it's kind of on purpose.
zh: 所以这算是——有一天我们也会在那边设办公室，但这多少是故意的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you feel you may miss anything by not having a foot there?
zh: 你觉得不在那边立足会错过什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, because we are over there very often, you know, we lived over there, we...
zh: 不会，因为我们经常去那边，你知道的，我们曾在那边生活过，我们……

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're still super connected to SF, and so you kind of benefit from the ecosystem anyway?
zh: 所以你们和 SF 仍然超级紧密连接，所以你们其实还是能从这个生态系统中受益？

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly, so I think it's...
zh: 完全正确，所以我觉得……

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amilabh is probably one of the most ambitious projects, probably the most ambitious projects you have ever done, but like, sounds very ambitious.
zh: Amilabh 可能是最有雄心的项目之一，可能是你做过的最有雄心的项目，但听起来非常有雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: How could you, what could you say to this room of talented kind of like...
zh: 你能对这屋子里有才华的、 kind of like……

speaker: Unknown
en: Builders who probably are picking on less ambitious ideas than yours.
zh: 这些可能在做的项目不如你的有雄心的建造者们，说点什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What could you tell them about how you learned about being ambitious?
zh: 关于你如何学会保持雄心，你能告诉他们什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And should they be that ambitious?
zh: 他们应该这么有雄心吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we are never enough, especially in France, in Europe, we are not ambitious enough.
zh: 我觉得我们永远不够，尤其是在法国、在欧洲，我们不够有雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a cliche, but it's true.
zh: 这是老生常谈，但这是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't take risks.
zh: 我们不冒险。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was telling you, you know, just one month after we were acquired by Facebook, I wanted to hire 100 people to do some kind of data annotation for machine learning.
zh: 我跟你说过，你知道的，就在我们被 Facebook 收购一个月后，我想雇 100 个人来做某种机器学习的数据标注。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mean like for WeDI?
zh: 你是说像是为了 WeDI？

speaker: Unknown
en: For WeDI, yeah.
zh: 为了 WeDI，对。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I wanted to hire 100 concierge who work for real customers, you know, to book travels, for instance, and record everything they do in order to train my model.
zh: 所以我想雇 100 个为真实客户服务的礼宾人员，你知道的，比如帮人订行程，并记录他们做的每件事，用来训练我的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was in 2015, 10 years ago.

speaker: Unknown
en: And I prepared the memo to ask the permission to Zuckerberg to hire 100 people who are not planning the budget.
zh: 我准备了备忘录，向 Zuckerberg 申请雇 100 个人，而且没规划进预算。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back then, there were 6,000 people at Facebook.
zh: 那时候 Facebook 有 6000 人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so 100 was not nothing.
zh: 是啊，所以 100 个人可不是小数目。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not nothing, you know, and 100 concierges in Menlo Park is expensive.
zh: 这可不是小事,你知道的,在门洛帕克雇 100 名礼宾员是很贵的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you meet Zuckerberg, you have to send a memo 24 hours before, at least, or your meeting is cancelled.
zh: 所以当你见到扎克伯格时,你必须至少提前 24 小时发一份备忘录,否则你的会议就会被取消。

speaker: Unknown
en: I arrived there and I was ready to argue to give every scientific argument why what I wanted to do was a great idea.
zh: 我到了那里,准备好争论,准备给出每一个科学论证,说明为什么我想做的事情是一个绝妙的主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I meet him and he tells me he had read the memo before and he tells me, Alex, I love the idea.
zh: 我见到他,他告诉我他之前已经读过那份备忘录了,他对我说,Alex,我喜欢这个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's great.
zh: 那太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we will kill Google because we will capture the intent and so with advertising and everything.
zh: 我认为我们会杀死 Google,因为我们会捕获用户意图,这样加上广告以及一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's hire 10,000 concierge, not 100.
zh: 所以我们雇 10,000 名礼宾员吧,不是 100 个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then I was, no, no, don't do that, actually.
zh: 然后我说,不,不,别那么做,其实。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had to tell him, no, no, no, Mark, actually, I'm not sure it will work.
zh: 我不得不告诉他,不,不,不,Mark,其实,我不确定这会奏效。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very dangerous.
zh: 这非常危险。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are lots of unknowns in this project, so we should not... To this day, I don't know if he was really willing to hire 10,000 people or if he thought it was the best way to get the real...
zh: 这个项目有很多未知数,所以我们不应该……直到今天,我也不知道他是真的愿意雇 10,000 人,还是他认为这是获取真实的……

speaker: Unknown
en: Information about what could go wrong in the project, but I loved the ambition A, and we hired 200.
zh: 关于这个项目可能出什么问题的信息的最好方式,但我喜欢这种雄心,A,我们雇了 200 人。

speaker: Unknown
en: 200 instead of 400, okay, like more than you expected.
zh: 200 而不是 400,好吧,比你预期的还多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, Marc has been well known for taking wild, crazy bets on stuff.
zh: 嗯,Marc 一直以在事情上下疯狂、大胆的赌注而闻名。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't, so I'm not that surprised he would go there, but yeah, kind of probably raised the bar from what you think is ambitious.
zh: 有时成功,有时不成功,所以我并不惊讶他会走到那一步,但是,是的,可能把你觉得算得上雄心勃勃的标准抬高了一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: What should the audience remember from that?
zh: 听众应该从中学到什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: How high should they aim at their stage?
zh: 在他们目前的阶段应该把目标定多高?

speaker: Unknown
en: At one point, people think too small when they're starting by trying to find a safe idea.
zh: 在某个时候,人们在起步时会想得太小,试图找一个安全的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or should they actually aim for something a lot more high potential, high risk?
zh: 还是说他们其实应该瞄准潜力大得多、风险也高得多的事情?

speaker: Unknown
en: If I could go back, you know, I think when you start, you should look at a very narrow problem, but be very, very ambitious in this narrow problem.
zh: 如果我能回到过去,你知道,我认为当你起步时,你应该看一个非常窄的问题,但在这个窄问题上要非常、非常雄心勃勃。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think including myself, the one thing I did wrong and I wanted to solve, to do a chatbot that does everything.
zh: 我想包括我自己在内,我做错的一件事就是,我想解决、想做一个什么都能做的聊天机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: For everyone, so not narrow.
zh: 面向所有人,所以不窄。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very, very hard to provide value as a very small team, small startup.
zh: 作为一个非常小的团队、小型创业公司,很难提供价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you choose a very narrow problem, like doing one thing for one industry or for one set of customers, but in this narrow tunnel, have a very big vision.
zh: 但如果你选择一个非常窄的问题,比如为一个行业或为一组客户做一件事,但在这个窄通道里,有一个非常大的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't be afraid to share your long-term vision.
zh: 不要害怕分享你的长期愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, I'm doing this today, but this is what we want to do later.
zh: 好的,我今天在做这件事,但这是我们以后想做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what I would do.
zh: 这是我会做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have only one life.
zh: 你只有一条命。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're young.
zh: 你还年轻。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you're very ambitious in a very wide field, then you're not credible.
zh: 但如果你在一个非常宽的领域里非常雄心勃勃,那你就没有可信度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Makes sense.
zh: 有道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just to conclude, if AMI works, no, when AMI will have worked, what will the world look like, like five, ten years from now?
zh: 最后总结一下,如果 AMI 成功了——不,当 AMI 成功之后,世界会是什么样子,比如五年、十年之后?

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you give us a glimpse of the future of your vision?
zh: 能让我们窥见一下你的愿景中的未来吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, first, I think we'll have robots, you know, helpful robots, actually helpful robots.
zh: 是的,首先,我认为我们会有机器人,你知道的,有用的机器人,真正有用的机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think most jobs will still be here, but not as dangerous or hard to do as they are today.
zh: 我认为大多数工作仍然会存在,但不会像今天这样危险或艰难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, I think machines with some sort of common sense will make a big difference.
zh: 而且,是的,我认为拥有某种常识的机器会带来巨大的改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much, Alex, for joining us today.
zh: 非常感谢你,Alex,今天加入我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks again.
zh: 再次感谢。
